name: Russia–NATO
summary: NATO commander warns Poland of possible Russian provocations on its north-east border
state: Polish PM Donald Tusk said on 3 Nov that NATO's top commander, Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, had warned of possible Russian provocations on Poland's north-eastern border; Poland deployed extra police and border units on 2 Nov and guards reported suspicious activity near Sępopol late on 3 Nov (Stars and Stripes; CBS News). No NATO member had requested Article 4 consultations as of 6 Nov.
for_you: No change for the public; follow official guidance if travelling near Poland's border with Kaliningrad.
rubric_hit: Explicit threats and border provocations; no Article 4 or clash

sources.title: Stars and Stripes — NATO's military chief tells Poland to keep wary eye on area near Russian border
CBS News — Poland launches major border operation

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
